subject: EVS
title: Living and Non-Living Things
summary: Living things grow, breathe, move on their own, and need food and water (e.g., children, dogs, trees, birds).
Non-living things do not grow or breathe on their own (e.g., stones, books, chairs, water).

glossary.kn: ನಿರ್ಜೀವ ವಸ್ತು (Does not grow or breathe)

examHotspots.q: Is a tree living or non-living?
examHotspots.a: Living—it grows bigger and needs water and sunlight.

flashcards.front: Does a toy car eat food or grow?

subject: Mathematics
title: Fractions — Halves and Quarters
summary: A fraction shows equal parts of a whole.
1/2 means one out of two equal parts (half); 1/4 means one out of four equal parts (quarter).

glossary.kn: ಕಾಲು ಭಾಗ (1 equal part out of 4)

examHotspots.q: If a roti is cut into 4 equal pieces and you eat 1 piece, what fraction is that?

subject: Science
title: Nutrition in Plants
summary: Autotrophic nutrition: Green plants make their own food using sunlight, water, carbon dioxide, and chlorophyll (photosynthesis).
Heterotrophic nutrition: Organisms that depend on others for food (e.g., animals, non-green plants).

examHotspots.q: Why are leaves called the food factories of plants?
examHotspots.a: Because photosynthesis takes place mainly in the leaves.

flashcards.front: Which gas is released during photosynthesis?

subject: Science
title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
summary: Chemical reactions form new substances with new properties (e.g., milk setting into curd, iron rusting).
Law of Conservation of Mass: Atoms are neither created nor destroyed, so equations must be balanced.
Main types: Combination, Decomposition, Displacement, and Double Displacement.

examHotspots.q: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned before burning in air?
examHotspots.a: To remove the protective oxide/carbonate layer so it burns smoothly.

examHotspots.q: Give one example each of exothermic and endothermic reactions.
examHotspots.a: Exothermic: Respiration / burning gas. Endothermic: Photosynthesis.

flashcards.front: What gas is released when zinc reacts with dilute HCl?
flashcards.back: Hydrogen gas (H₂) — burns with a 'pop' sound.

flashcards.front: Which gas is flushed in chips packets to prevent rancidity?

subject: Mathematics
title: Polynomials
summary: A polynomial p(x) of degree n has at most n zeroes.
Graphically, zeroes are x-coordinates where y = p(x) cuts or touches the x-axis.
For ax² + bx + c (a ≠ 0): Sum of zeroes = -b/a and Product of zeroes = c/a.

examHotspots.q: Find sum and product of zeroes of 2x² - 8x + 6.

flashcards.front: Maximum number of zeroes of a cubic polynomial?
